text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Canada setting salmon quotas: Fleet awaits word from Ottawa as Axworthy proposes arbitration.
- Private bid for TVO weighed: Not-for-profit pitch revealed.
- Supreme Court faces integrity issue: Hearing explores implications of halting war-crimes over judge's conduct.
- Another Morin witness recants on stand: Slain child's best friend says police helped shape her testimony.
- Top U.S. court defends Internet freedom: Supreme Court strikes down two provisions of 1996 law controlling on-line pornography.
- Onex wins bid for BC Sugar: Belkins join in surprise C$415-million takeover offer and Pattison agrees to tender his stake.
- Central bank raises key rate to defend dollar: Stocks and bonds pay the price for quarter-point increase.
- Inco, union reach deal: Four-week strike at nickel giant could be over by Saturday.
- Royal faces C$1-billion good-will charge if it wins London Life: Could put bank at odds with regulator.
- Bank of Canada rate hike blindsides markets.
- Lightning bid wins BC Sugar: Onex Corp. joins Stuart Belkin in 11th-hour offer worth C$415 million. Rival Jim Pattison throws in the towel. BC Sugar directors endorse new bid.
